text:
devon: seeing a handful of pod-to-pod gRPC streams in eu-west-1 repeatedly stall and recover. p50 token latency spikes from 40ms -> 2s then back. Not CPU. Suspect packet fragmentation + retransmits. :thinking:

jordan: which pods/services? any common node pairs or NICs?

devon: gpu-infer-* pods on nodepool-gpu-a -> nodepool-gpu-b, mostly for long-lived streaming RPCs (grpc 1.55). Happened after the calico IPPool change yesterday.

maria: can you paste `ip link` and `ip -d link` from one of the affected nodes? also `dmesg` for any frag or ipfrag warnings.

devon: quick captures:
```
# on node A
ip link show eth0
2: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether ...
# on node B
ip link show eth0
2: eth0: mtu 1450 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
and tcpdump shows lots of retransmits and occasional ICMP "Fragmentation needed" from the overlay interface.

sam: ahhh differing host MTU between node pairs -> VXLAN/Geneve overhead + calico IPIP/encap results in packets that exceed path MTU, kernel sends back ICMP frag-needed but some overlays drop them so Linux falls back poorly and TCP stalls. gRPC streaming is sensitive because streams keep the connection open and use large payloads.

maria: any iptables/mangle rules that might be blocking ICMP? that would prevent PMTU discovery from working.

devon: checked, no coarse ICMP DROP rules in our egress chain. But calico changed default `vxlanMTU` when the new pool got applied; nodepool-gpu-a still had the old MTU (1500) at host level, nodepool-gpu-b got reset to 1450 as part of the upgrade.

jordan: that mismatch would cause exactly this. packets leaving node A are 1500, encapsulated -> 1500 + 50 = exceeds 1450 path -> frag-needed from B, but overlay path blackholes some ICMP. result: gRPC sender keeps sending, kernel retransmits and stalls.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2024-0819 created for eu-west-1 streaming stalls (assigned: @maria, priority: P2).

sam: short-term mitigation options:
- set `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on affected nodes (enables TCP to probe smaller MTU automatically)
- set host MTU uniformly to 1450 on both sides (`ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1450`) to match CNI encap overhead
- temporarily disable VXLAN encapsulation (if safe) or set calico Pool mtu to 1450 and roll nodes in small batches

maria: pros/cons: tcp_mtu_probing helps but causes extra probe traffic and can still be slow for long-lived high-throughput streams. Changing host MTU is deterministic and lower-risk if we can roll nodepool with churn control. Disabling encap would be risky for network policy.

devon: tried `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` on one pair, latency spikes reduced and stream resumed, but throughput dropped ~10%. Verified with a short curl to grpc gateway and `strace` shows fewer EAGAINs.

jordan: we should also consider offload interactions. if one host has GSO/TSO/GRO enabled and the other doesn't, you can see large skbs that get chopped by the NIC leading to odd retransmits. `ethtool -k eth0` check on both nodes.

sam: commands we ran:
```
# check MTU and routes
ip link show eth0 && ip route get 10.100.5.8
# enable probing
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
# unify MTU
ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1450
# toggle offloads (debug only)
ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off
```

maria: plan: 1) run `ethtool -k` and `ip link` checks across nodepool-gpu-a/b, 2) enable tcp_mtu_probing on all gpu nodes as immediate mitigator (can be rolled back), 3) schedule controlled nodepool reboot to set host MTU=1450 (cluster autoscaler drained nodes one at a time), 4) update calico IPPool `vxlanMTU` and in our infra repo to avoid future drift.

devon: +1 to plan. will open a PR to infra repo with the calico pool MTU change and a k8s nodepool migration playbook.

oncall-bot: Pager duty alert suppressed (policy: streaming-degraded-eu-west).

jordan: follow-up: add a kubelet startup check asserting host MTU == configured calico MTU and warn in node labels so scheduler can avoid mixed-MTU pods. small script suggestion: `if [ $(cat /sys/class/net/eth0/mtu) -ne $CALICO_MTU ]; then echo "mtu-mismatch" > /var/lib/node-problem-detector/conditions; fi`

sam: we'll also add a Grafana panel for ICMP frag-needed counters (from node exporter) and a small e2e test that runs stress-ng TCP streaming across nodepairs to catch regressions.

maria: assigning follow-ups: INC-2024-0819 (investigation), INFRA-2557 (calico mtu PR), INFRA-2558 (nodepool rollout), SRE-3120 (Grafana alert).

devon: thanks all. restarting canary rollout now for nodepool-gpu-a with `mtu=1450` and will report back in 30m. :thumbsup:
